The '''Estonian Mathematical Society''' (Estonian: {{lang|et|Eesti Matemaatika Selts}}, '''EMS''') is a [[mathematical society]] founded in Estonia in February 1926.
The EMS is based in [[Tartu]], and is a founding member of the [[European Mathematical Society]].{{r|ems2001|ems-members}} It is recognised by the [[International Mathematical Union]].{{r|imu}}

==History==
[[File:Gerhard Rägo, 1920s.jpg|thumb|Gerhard Rägo (pictured in the 1920s) was the first president of the Estonian Mathematical Society.]]
The predecessor of the Estonian Mathematical Society was the Academic Mathematical Society (Estonian: {{lang|et|Akadeemiline Matemaatika Selts}}), which was founded in Tartu on 23 February 1926.{{r|ems2001}}

In 1940 Estonia was annexed by the [[Soviet Union]] and became the [[Estonian SSR]].{{r|malksoo}}
The Academic Mathematical Society was forced to cease its activities, and had its last meeting in November 1940.{{r|ems2001}}
[[Hans Kruus]], who was at the time rector of the [[University of Tartu]], recommended that the society be dissolved, but this was prevented from happening when [[Operation Barbarossa]] (and the subsequent occupation of Estonia by the Nazis) shifted the priorities of the Soviet Union.{{r|ems2001}}
Society president {{ill|Hermann Jaakson|et}} repeatedly tried to restart the activities of the society during the war, but was unsuccessful.{{r|ems2001}}

When the Second World War ended scientific societies continued to be banned in Estonia.{{r|ems2001}}
An attempt to restart the society in 1983 was rejected by the [[Communist Party of Estonia]].{{r|ems2001}}
In 1987 the Soviet Union introduced ''[[perestroika]]'', which allowed for more political independence.
On 17 September 1987 the Academic Mathematical Society held its re-opening conference, and its name was changed to the Estonian Mathematical Society.{{r|ems2001}}

In April 1988 a Computer Science branch of the EMS was established. It was disbanded in 1993 following the formation of the Estonian Society of Informatics.{{r|history}}

==Awards==
===Arnold Humal Prize===
The Estonian Mathematical Society annually awards the Arnold Humal Prize to an Estonian mathematician under the age of 30.
Because {{ill|Arnold Humal|et}} obtained his PhD at the age of 26, the prize decides between equal candidates in favour of the younger.{{r|Humal-prize}}
Past winners of the prize are:{{r|Humal-prize}}
{{div col|colwidth=18em}}
*2007 – Kristel Mikkor
*2009 – Helle Visk
*2010 – Evely Leetma
*2011 – Daria Gordon
*2012 – Indrek Zolk
*2013 – Aleksei Lissitsin
*2014 – Erge Ideon
*2016 – Johann Langemets
*2017 – Silja Veidenberg
*2019 – Ülo Reimaa
*2021 – Rihhard Nadel
*2023 – Kristo Väljako and Andre Ostrak
{{div col end}}

===Other awards===
The EMS Publication Award (Estonian: {{lang|et|EMS Publikatsiooniauhind}}) is awarded to a young mathematician with a connection to Estonia for a publication in an international mathematical journal.{{r|pub-award}}

The Professor Gerhard Rägo Memorial Medal has since 1990 been awarded for improving the teaching of mathematics in Estonian schools.{{r|Rago-medal}}

The Student Prize of the EMS (Estonian: {{lang|et|Eesti Matemaatika Seltsi üliõpilaspreemia}}) is a scholarship awarded annually to recognise "meaningful results obtained by students in their undergraduate studies in mathematics and applications of mathematics."{{r|student-prize}}

The Olaf Prinitsa Prize recognises a student who has obtained a master's degree in mathematics education.{{r|Prinitsa-prize}}

==Presidents==
Past presidents of the Estonian Mathematical Society are: {{r|ems2001}}
{{div col}}
*{{ill|Gerhard Rägo|et}} (1926–1927)
*[[Jüri Nuut]] (1927–1932)
*[[Edgar Krahn]] (1932–1936)
*{{ill|Hermann Jaakson|et}} (1936–1940)
*[[Ülo Lumiste]] (1987–1993)
*{{ill|Mati Abel|et}} (1994–2003){{r|Abel}}
*{{ill|Kalle Kaarli|et}} (2003–2009){{r|activities-2002-3|Kaarli-cv}}
*Raul Kangro (elected 2009){{r|activities-2009}}
*Valdis Laan (2015–2018){{r|activities-2013-6|Laan-cv}}
*{{ill|Rainis Haller|et}} (2018−2022){{r|activities-2018|Haller-cv}}
*Jüri Lember (2021–present){{r|ems-info|Lember-cv}}
{{div col end}}
